hook.text: A store offered 24 jams—shoppers bought less. Six varieties—sales tripled. More choices killed the joy of choosing.

buildup.text: Barry Schwartz calls this the 'paradox of choice.' More options increase anxiety and decrease satisfaction.

discovery.text: Every option creates a counterfactual: 'What if I'd picked the other one?' Regret lurks behind every good choice.

twist.text: Societies with fewer choices report higher satisfaction. Constraints protect joy by reducing comparison opportunities.

climax.text: 'Satisficers' who pick 'good enough' are happier than 'maximizers' who seek the best. Perfection kills joy.

punchline.text: More options, less joy. The best choice is to stop choosing.
